headline: Highest risk is medium: caveman’s MCP/file-based outputs can be consumed by awesome-nlp with no documented isolation, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly uses MCP and file surfaces (CLAUDE.md, project notes), while awesome-nlp has no isolation or parser controls documented. That makes a shared-content pathway plausible in default use, even though awesome-nlp is not runnable and no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman content is copied into a shared workspace or MCP-fed prompt that awesome-nlp later reads as text, injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator routes caveman-generated notes into awesome-nlp without provenance filtering, instructions can be smuggled.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared notes into prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to all caveman-generated files.
Review any copied text before passing it to awesome-nlp.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or allowlist parsing between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network egress none, and no secrets or sensitive data classes are declared for awesome-nlp. caveman does touch session logs and memory files, but there is no documented shared filesystem or upload path to a third party. The pair therefore has a limited leakage pathway unless the operator creates one.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing session logs or memory files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is configured to export files outside the local machine, the pair can expose those files.
mitigations: Store session logs in a separate directory.
Do not place secrets in caveman memory files.
Verify both agents remain local-only.
Rotate any accidentally shared notes.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs or per-agent sandboxes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or concurrency surfaces documented, while caveman supports multiple instances and touches files. Without a shared writable target, direct conflict is not established. The main risk is operator-created overlap, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF caveman instances run concurrently against the same notes, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one caveman instance per workspace.
Use timestamped filenames.
Check for duplicate writes before merging.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that can become downstream input, while awesome-nlp has no documented verification layer or critical-evaluation behavior. That creates a plausible default pathway where one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, even though the exact orchestration is undocumented.
conditions: IF caveman-generated notes are fed into awesome-nlp as instructions or facts, downstream errors can cascade.
IF an operator uses awesome-nlp outputs to rewrite caveman project notes without review, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs.
Mark generated text as untrusted.
Separate fact extraction from action execution.
Compare outputs against source material.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and consumption.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling mismatch is documented for either profile. awesome-nlp touches no data classes, and caveman’s declared data classes are generic operational artifacts rather than regulated categories. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either profile is later documented to handle regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance exposure.
IF a deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here, compliance risk may change.
mitigations: Confirm data-class scope before deployment.
Avoid placing regulated data in either agent.
Document retention settings.
Review vendor residency requirements.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
